page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-32xCPU-384GB is a Cloud Native family server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with 32 physical cores and 32 vCPUs, operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The CPU allocation is shared, and the processor includes 64 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of memory, yielding 12.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include any local storage or GPU hardware, but it does provide one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals distinct performance characteristics and tradeoffs. Single-core performance is a notable bottleneck, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance scoring in the bottom 10% (748.19) and single-threaded gzip compression rated in the bottom 25% (23.67 GB/sec). However, multi-threaded capabilities are significantly stronger, as evidenced by a strong top 25% rating in bzip3 multi-threaded decompression (228.74 GB/sec) and Geekbench multi-core scores (17094.0). Memory bandwidth remains stable in the middle 50% tier, registering 131.44 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 82.64 GB/sec for large block write operations.

Given the shared CPU allocation and the high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 12 GB per core, this server offers a cost-efficient profile for memory-intensive workloads that can tolerate shared CPU resources. It is suitable for large-scale caching layers, database operations, and multi-threaded text processing, where Geekbench text processing scored in the top 25% (2449.0). It is less suited for single-threaded tasks or workloads requiring dedicated CPU performance and local NVMe storage.
